skill.name: casely
skill.description: Generate QA test cases from requirements, examples, and style guides. Casely parses documents, plans coverage, creates atomic test cases, and exports Excel files.
skill.summary: Generate style-matched QA test cases and Excel exports from project requirements.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around slash commands, file names, and paths. The real concerns are package-manager execution, unpinned dependency installation, and bundled script execution for parsing and export workflows.

remediation.issue: Package manager commands can install mutable dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before uv init, uv add, or uv sync, and pin dependencies or provide a reviewed lockfile.

remediation.issue: Parser and exporter workflows execute bundled Python scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Document exact scripts, arguments, and expected file access, and require confirmation before running them on project files.

content.user_title: Generate QA Test Cases from Requirements
content.value_statement: QA teams spend significant time converting requirements into consistent test cases. Casely parses project documents, learns example formats, and exports structured cases.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a project workspace with input, processed, results, and exports folders.
Converts PDF, DOCX, and XLSX requirement documents to Markdown through Docling.
Builds a style guide from example test cases and preserves column order.
Plans QA coverage by module, level, risk, and estimated case count.
Generates one atomic Markdown test case per scenario using the selected test type.
Exports generated Markdown test cases to one Excel file per case.
limitations: Requires local Python tooling and uv before parsing or exporting can run.
Quality depends on clear requirements and representative example test cases.
Does not verify generated tests against the live product or test environment.
May need review before import into strict Test Management Systems.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Test Cases
use_cases.description: Derive columns and writing style from approved examples before generating cases for a release.

use_cases.title: Draft Cases from Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into functional, negative, boundary, and integration cases with less repetitive writing.

use_cases.title: Prepare TMS Import Files
use_cases.description: Create Excel-ready case files while preserving one scenario per source file.

prompt_templates.title: Start a QA Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize a new Casely project named BillingPortal and tell me where to place requirements and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Parse Requirement Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Parse the latest project documents and summarize which files were converted, skipped, or failed.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Style Guide and Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my example cases, create the style guide, then plan critical coverage for the checkout module.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Export Targeted Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate negative and integration cases for the payment retry flow, then export the results to Excel.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer starts a BillingPortal project with requirement PDFs and example Excel cases.
output: The assistant tells the user where to place files.
The next step suggests parsing documents.

output_examples.input: A team asks for negative test cases for password reset requirements.
output_examples.output: Casely creates separate Markdown cases, each with one table row that matches the style guide.

output_examples.input: A test manager exports generated login cases.
output_examples.output: The export folder receives one Excel file per test case with the original columns preserved.

best_practices: Review the generated style guide before generating cases.
Use representative example cases with the exact columns your team needs.
Generate critical cases first, then expand to negative, boundary, and integration coverage.
anti_patterns: Do not generate cases before parsing requirements and approving the style guide.
Do not mix unrelated modules in one generation request.
Do not import exported files into a TMS without a QA review.

faq.question: What does Casely generate?
faq.answer: It generates QA plans, Markdown test cases, and Excel exports based on your requirements and examples.

faq.question: Can it read PDF, DOCX, and XLSX files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Docling for document parsing and openpyxl for Excel export support.

faq.question: Does it create one large test suite file?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to create one atomic test case file per scenario.

faq.question: Can it match our test format?
faq.answer: Yes. It builds a style guide from examples and uses that guide for columns and wording.

faq.question: Does it run commands on my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. Parsing and export workflows use local Python scripts and uv-managed dependencies.

faq.question: Is generated content ready to import?
faq.answer: It can produce import-ready Excel files, but QA review is recommended before TMS upload.
